name: Palmyra Palm
notes: The tala, the fan palm of the dry plains, standing alone or in lines along a field's edge. Its leaves are the leaves the old books are written on: cut, boiled, dried and scored. Its leaf-stalks give a coarse fibre that twists into rope, and it yields the same husk the date palm does. Added so that the Narmada's archive grows its own pages and Dwarka's harbour rope has a palm on the plains to come from.
journal_prompt: A fan of leaves on a straight black trunk. Somebody has cut the lowest fronds, neatly, and taken them away to write on.
